issues.legal_issue: A general customary-law digest that leaves the existence of a local custom uncertain is of limited assistance in deciding whether that custom exists.
material_facts: The parties were Hindu Jats, and the dispute concerned whether their community recognized divorce and remarriage.
The digest described custom as varying among tribes and localities and noted doubt about whether the claimed custom existed in the relevant district.
issues.conclusion: The digest did not establish whether the claimed custom existed in the community concerned and was of little assistance in deciding that question.
issues.legal_principle: Custom may vary by tribe and locality, so a general digest does not establish a local custom where it leaves the local position uncertain. The Court considered Rattigan's Digest of Customary Law, including its recognition that special customs could differ from the general rule.

predicates.custom_proof_proceeding: The dispute required a court to decide whether a particular community custom existed.
predicates.digest_leaves_local_custom_unresolved: The customary-law digest discussed the subject generally but left the existence of the claimed local custom uncertain.

issues.definition: When a dispute requires proof of a community custom and the digest leaves the local custom unresolved, the digest is not determinative.

issues.legal_issue: An unreliable customary record that is contradicted by evidence cannot establish the absence of a custom.
material_facts: The local customary record stated that divorce was not recognized among Hindus, subject to a stated exception for another community.
Courts had previously found the record unreliable because it had not been prepared with care and attention.
Witnesses for both sides acknowledged that a husband could divorce his wife in the community, and evidence contradicted the record's statement that no such custom existed.
issues.conclusion: The local customary record was unreliable and could not be relied on to establish that the claimed custom did not exist.
issues.legal_principle: A customary record may carry an initial presumption of correctness if it is reliable and trustworthy; the weight of evidence required to rebut that presumption depends on the circumstances. An unreliable record has no presumptive value. The Court relied on Mahant Salig Ram v. Musammat Maya Devi and the criteria approved there from Qamar-ud-Din v. Mt. Fateh Bano, as well as Mohammad Khalil v. Mohammad Bakhsh and the cited decisions finding the local record unreliable.

predicates.custom_proof_proceeding: The dispute required a court to decide whether a particular community custom existed.
predicates.customary_record_previously_found_unreli: Courts had found the customary record insufficiently careful or trustworthy.
predicates.evidence_contradicts_record: Testimony or other evidence in the case showed that the record's statement about the custom was incorrect.

issues.definition: When a proceeding requires proof of a custom, a previously unreliable customary record contradicted by the evidence does not have presumptive evidentiary force.

issues.legal_issue: A custom permitting divorce and remarriage may be established by evidence of the custom in surrounding communities together with oral testimony and instances of its exercise.
material_facts: The customary records of districts surrounding the district in question recorded a custom of divorce among Hindu Jats.
Witnesses testified that the community recognized a husband's right to divorce his wife and that divorced women could remarry while their first husbands were alive.
Witnesses described instances of divorced women contracting second marriages that the community recognized as valid.
Even witnesses called by the opposing party acknowledged a custom permitting a husband to divorce his wife.
issues.conclusion: The evidence supported the finding that the community custom permitted divorce and allowed a divorced woman to remarry during her first husband's lifetime.
issues.legal_principle: Custom is primarily tribal, though it may vary by locality; accordingly, evidence of a custom among the same tribe in surrounding districts is relevant to whether it exists locally. Oral testimony and proved instances of the custom may support the finding. The Court considered Rattigan's discussion of tribal custom and relied on the evidence accepted by the High Court.

predicates.custom_proof_proceeding: The dispute required a court to decide whether a particular community custom existed.
predicates.surrounding_communities_share_custom: Communities of the same tribe in surrounding areas were shown to follow the claimed custom.
predicates.oral_evidence_supports_custom: Witnesses testified that the community followed the claimed custom.
predicates.instances_show_custom_exercised: Evidence described actual cases in which community members acted in accordance with the claimed custom.

issues.definition: When a custom is disputed, evidence that surrounding communities share it, supported by testimony and actual instances, supports recognition of a custom permitting divorce and remarriage.

issues.legal_issue: A valid customary divorce permits the divorced woman to remarry during her former husband's lifetime, and a marriage entered into under that custom entitles her to succeed as the deceased husband's widow.
material_facts: The woman's first husband executed a document divorcing her.
The woman subsequently married the deceased by a customary form of marriage while her first husband was alive.
The established community custom permitted divorce and recognized the validity of remarriage by a divorced woman during her first husband's lifetime.
The deceased acknowledged the woman as his wife and left his property to her; after his death, she claimed the property as his widow.
issues.conclusion: The divorce was valid, the subsequent marriage was valid, and the woman was entitled to succeed to the deceased husband's property as his widow.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proved custom, a valid divorce dissolved the former marriage; once it was dissolved, the divorced woman could remarry during the former husband's lifetime. The Court applied Rattigan's statement that remarriage is barred only until the former marriage is validly set aside, and held that the proven custom recognized the second marriage. The Court consequently upheld the widow's entitlement to the property.

predicates.customary_marriage_dispute: The proceeding concerned whether a marriage contracted after a customary divorce was valid and conferred spousal succession rights.
predicates.valid_customary_divorce: The first marriage was validly dissolved under a custom recognized in the community.
predicates.custom_allows_remarriage_during_former_h: The community custom permits a divorced woman to remarry while her former husband is alive.
predicates.second_marriage_contracts_under_custom: The woman entered into the later marriage in the manner recognized by the community custom.

issues.definition: When a valid customary divorce is followed by a marriage permitted and contracted under the community custom, the later marriage is valid and the surviving spouse succeeds as a widow.
